newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN LEADS U.S. OPEN AFTER THREE ROUNDS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN LEADS U.S. OPEN AFTER THREE ROUNDS.

text.p: Tom Lehman birdied the final hole of the rain-delayed third round of the U.S. Open early on Sunday to take a two-stroke lead into the day's final round.

Second-round leader Lehman, who carded a two-under-par 68 for a five-under total of 205, stood two better than Jeff Maggert, who had led the rain-interrupted round overnight, and Ernie Els, who jumped into contention with three birdies in the five holes he played on Sunday morning.
Colin Montgomerie, who had led the first round, was the only other player under par entering the last round after posting a 67, the lowest score of the third round.
Masters champion Tiger Woods, meanwhile, appeared to have ruined any chance to continue a Grand Slam run as he finished the round at four over par, nine shots off the pace.

They were among 21 players who had to complete the third round early on Sunday after a thunderstorm struck Congressional Country Club on Saturday, forcing a two-hour delay of play for the second consecutive day. Friday's second round was also interrupted by bad weather and had to be concluded on Saturday morning.

Maggert, who had wrested the third-round lead from Lehman before the storm struck, fell back with a bogey on Congressional's scenic signature hole -- the 480-yard, par-4 17th, which finishes on the shore of a lake that is shared by the 18th hole. He matched Lehman's 68.
Els, the big South African who won the 1994 Open in a three-man playoff, caught Maggert with three consecutive birdies from the 15th to shoot 69 and stand two shots from the lead.

The final round began immediately after the third ended on a pleasant, sunny morning, a welcome change from the previous two rainy days. There were 84 players still in the field with the final pairing of the day -- Lehman and Maggert -- due to tee off at 2:54 p.m. (1854 GMT).
Jay Haas (68), Tommy Tolles (69) and David Ogrin (71) were all at level-par 210.

Montgomerie, who lost to Els in the '94 playoff, had to play only two holes in the early morning light, but the smooth-swinging Scot could not gain on the leaders, making a bogey on the 17th and then a birdie on the 190-yard 18th -- the first par-three to conclude an Open since 1909.

Woods, who has found the 7,213-yard, par-70 Congressional far harder than Augusta National, also played two holes in the morning, parring both for a 73 that left him nine strokes adrift in his quest for a seventh consecutive U.S. national championship.
Woods, who had won the Masters with a record total score in April, had won three consecutive U.S. Junior and three successive U.S. Amateur championships.
However, the 21-year-old crowd pleaser had his work cut out for him in the final round, where 20 players stood between him and his second consecutive major championship.
